title: The Smallest String After Allowed Swaps

concept.title: Swappable positions form groups; inside a group any order is possible, so sort it
body: You may swap the letters at the positions of any given pair, any number of times. If you can swap positions `a` and `b`, and also `b` and `c`, then you can bring the letters of `a`, `b` and `c` into **any order** (swapping neighbours in a chain gives every permutation). So the positions fall into **groups** connected through the pairs, and inside a group the letters can be arranged freely.

To get the lexicographically smallest string, arrange the letters inside every group in **increasing order along the positions of the group**: the smallest letter at the smallest position, and so on. Nothing else can be improved.
Sorting all groups costs O(n log n) in total. The same "connected positions can be permuted freely" argument solves several swap puzzles.

statement: A string `s` of length `n` and `m` pairs of positions are given. In one operation you can swap the letters at the two positions of any pair; you may use the operations as often as you like and in any order. Print the lexicographically smallest string you can make.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the length of the string and the number of pairs.
The second line has the string `s` of `n` lowercase letters.
Each of the next `m` lines has two positions `a` and `b` (counted from 1): the letters at these positions may be swapped, as often as you like.

examples.note: The positions {1, 4} hold d and b, and {2, 3} hold c and a. Sorted inside the groups: b a c d.

hints: Use union-find to group the positions that are connected through the pairs.
Collect the positions of every group (in increasing order) and the letters at them.
Sort the letters and write them back to the positions of the group in order.

explanation: Union-find groups the positions connected by pairs; inside each group the letters are sorted and written back to the positions of the group in increasing order.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + m) alpha(n) + n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

parent = []
size = []

def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

def union(a, b):
    a, b = find(a), find(b)
    if a == b:
        return False
    if size[a] < size[b]:
        a, b = b, a
    parent[b] = a
    size[a] += size[b]
    return True

n, m = map(int, input().split())
s = input().strip()
pairs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

parent.extend(range(n))
size.extend([1] * n)
for a, b in pairs:
    union(a - 1, b - 1)
groups = {}
for i in range(n):
    groups.setdefault(find(i), []).append(i)
result = list(s)
for positions in groups.values():
    letters = sorted(s[i] for i in positions)
    for i, letter in zip(positions, letters):
        result[i] = letter
print("".join(result))
